---
# Refreshes the people on maester.dev/sponsor: the contributors who have a GitHub Sponsors listing.
name: Update sponsor page

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 3 * * 1" # Mondays 03:17 UTC
  push:
    branches: ["main"]
    paths:
      - "website/contributors/contributors.yml"
      - "website/scripts/sponsors.mjs"
      - ".github/workflows/update-sponsors.yaml"

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: update-sponsors
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  update-sponsors:
    name: Update sponsor page
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read

    steps:
      # The maester-bot app, not GITHUB_TOKEN: it looks up the Sponsors listing of each contributor over
      # GraphQL and opens the pull request, which then runs the checks of the repository.
      - name: Generate maester-bot app token
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.MAESTER_BOT_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.MAESTER_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24.x
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: website/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: website
        run: npm ci

      - name: Look up Sponsors listings
        working-directory: website
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: node scripts/sponsors.mjs

An audit of the current site, a recommended stack, a plan that keeps our search ranking, a new information architecture, the home page story, and the Ask Maester assistant with Sign in with ChatGPT. Nothing has been changed yet.

Open the mocks → 6 mocks: home, docs, test page, catalog, Ask Maester, design language Updated: HyperFrames explainers
Summary What I found SEO: what we must keep Stack: Astro or Docusaurus Docs layout Home page and marketing Ask Maester Explainers (HyperFrames) Design language GitHub Actions Plan and phases Decisions for you

Summary

StackRebuild on Astro 6 with Starlight, styled with maester.cloud's tokens. maester.cloud already runs Astro 6 and Tailwind 4, so all three sites can share one design package. Docusaurus can be re-themed, but it would still hydrate React on every page and keep the versioning model that causes our duplicate URLs.
SEOKeep every indexed path. Fix the redirect that every one of our 2,679 sitemap URLs goes through today. Fold the 1,033 duplicate /docs/next pages into /docs. Redirect the ~665 command pages that 3.0 removes. Add a CI check that fails the build if any old URL breaks.
DocsMintlify-style top tabs (Guides · Test catalog · Commands · Packs · Changelog), seven plain sidebar groups that follow the path from quickstart to automation, and a filterable test catalog in place of seven 100-to-300-item sidebars.
HomeThe 3.0 story: every framework in one run, Microsoft's Zero Trust Assessment inside the report, Maester Packs, automation, and Maester Cloud for history and drift. Every number comes from the catalog at build time.
ExplainersShort animated explainers made with HyperFrames (HTML and GSAP, rendered to video) for the concepts that are hard to follow in text: how a run works, gates and reason codes, config layers, packs, the Zero Trust Assessment. One sits on the home page, and the rest sit inline in the docs page each one explains.
Ask MaesterDay one: Copy page, Open in ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot, Markdown for every page, llms.txt and a Maester docs MCP server. None of these need approval. Sign in with ChatGPT comes next: OpenAI offers it to websites as a limited trial, so we apply now and turn it on when they approve.

Home page and marketing

The home page's job is to show, in one scroll, what Maester gives someone running Microsoft 365. The Home page board has the full draft:

  1. Hero: "Test your Microsoft 365 security, every day, in one run", the install command, Quickstart, and a report mock in place of the old GIF.
  2. Proof: 625K+ PowerShell Gallery downloads, 1,177 checks, 1.2K GitHub stars and 72 contributors, all read at build time.
  3. Coverage: CIS, CISA SCuBA, Zero Trust Assessment, EIDSCA, ORCA, Active Directory and Maester checks, with real counts, plus MITRE ATT&CK and NIST mapping.
  4. Zero Trust Assessment: its own band. Microsoft's assessment, 336 results across six pillars, in the same report.
  5. How it works: install, connect, run, automate, each with its one command.
  6. What's new in 3.0: the engine, tests in the module, selection, reason codes, layered config, packs.
  7. Automate, Maester Packs (real cards from packs.maester.cloud), Write your own (a native test).
  8. Maester Cloud: history, drift and many tenants, with a reminder that subscriptions keep the core free.
  9. Community: contributors, Discord, sponsor, manifesto.

Beyond the home page I'd add landing pages built for search: /frameworks/cis, /frameworks/cisa-scuba and /zero-trust-assessment. Each explains the framework, lists its checks from the catalog and shows the one command that runs them. These target searches such as "CIS Microsoft 365 benchmark automation", where we have the best answer and no landing page today.

Explainers with HyperFrames

HyperFrames is HeyGen's open-source framework (Apache 2.0) for making video from HTML: a composition is an HTML page with CSS for the look, a GSAP timeline for the motion and data-* attributes for timing. It ships agent skills for Claude Code, so we can write and revise explainers the same way we write the docs. The Home page board has a working chapter player for "the life of a run", and the Docs page board shows an inline explainer for gates and reason codes.

How it fits the site

  1. Source in the repository. Each explainer is a folder, website/explainers/<slug>/index.html, built from our design tokens, so it matches the site in both themes. The text in it comes from the same facts as the docs; a reviewer can read the HTML in a pull request.
  2. Rendered in CI. A workflow runs npx hyperframes render (Node 22+, FFmpeg, headless Chrome) when an explainer changes. It produces an MP4, a WebM, a poster frame and a captions file, and opens a pull request like the blog-cards workflow does. The video files go to Cloudflare R2 rather than into git.
  3. An <Explainer> component in the docs. It shows the poster with a play button, chapter markers, captions and a "Transcript" toggle. It never autoplays, and with reduced motion it shows the poster and transcript only. HyperFrames also has an embeddable <hyperframes-player> component; I'd test it in phase 1, because playing the HTML live would be crisper and lighter than video.
  4. Search and AI. Each explainer page carries the full transcript as text and VideoObject JSON-LD, so search engines and Ask Maester can read what the video says. The same MP4s can go on YouTube for reach.

The first explainers

ExplainerWhere it livesWhat it shows
Maester in 60 secondsHome page heroInstall, connect, run, report, automate, ending on the report
The life of a runHome page, Core conceptsConfig → selection → gates → engine → report (in the mock)
Gates and reason codesChoose what to run, Read the reportWhy a check was skipped, gate by gate (in the mock)
Configuration layersConfigure Maester, Many tenantsA tenant file merging over the base file, key by key
FamiliesNative test referenceOne check becoming one row per policy or mailbox
Installing a packPacksScan → cooldown → policy → pin → approve → lock file
The Zero Trust Assessment in MaesterFrameworks, Packs, home page bandA separate PowerShell process, the results mapped to ZTA rows, one report
No secrets in your pipelineAutomateWorkload identity federation from GitHub or Azure DevOps to Entra
Maester and Maester CloudHome page Cloud bandRuns flowing into history, drift and alerts
The 3.0 launch post already has hand-built components for the run pipeline and the gates (Pipeline and Gates in its _components.jsx). Their wording is the script for the first two explainers.

Plan and phases

The durations are rough estimates for one person with Claude, to show scale.

PhaseWorkRough size
0. NowFix the trailing-slash redirect on the current site. Fill in OpenAI's interest form. Export Search Console data for the URL contract.A day
1. FoundationDesign package, Astro and Starlight skeleton, overrides, Pagefind, redirect map, URL-contract check1–2 weeks
2. ContentPort and restructure the guides; catalog and test pages from JSON; commands; 25 blog posts; React islands2–3 weeks
3. MarketingHome page, framework and Zero Trust pages, packs page1 week
3b. ExplainersExplainer component and render workflow; the run, gates and Zero Trust explainers first, then the rest one at a time1 week, then about a day each
4. Ask Maester, layer 1Markdown routes, llms.txt, Copy page menu, MCP Worker1 week
5. LaunchIdeally with 3.0 GA, so /docs switches to 3.0 and the redirects land once. Watch Search Console for four weeks.—
6. Ask Maester, layer 2Sign in with ChatGPT, retrieval index, panel1–2 weeks after approval

Decisions for you

Recommend: Astro + Starlight1. Stack

Astro and Starlight sharing maester.cloud's design package, or a re-theme of Docusaurus.

Recommend: with 3.0 GA2. Launch timing

Launch with 3.0 GA, so the version switch and the redirects happen once, or earlier with 2.3 as the default.

Recommend: frozen archive, noindex3. 2.x docs

Keep a frozen copy at /docs/2.x/, or drop it and redirect everything to 3.0.

Recommend: apply now4. Sign in with ChatGPT

Fill in OpenAI's interest form for maester.dev, and decide whether to fund a fallback quota if they decline.

Recommend: ship it this week5. Trailing-slash fix

Fix the redirect on today's site as its own small PR before the rebuild.

Your call6. Stats and analytics

The old home page claims "60K+ tenants protected". Should we keep it, and if so, from what source? Should Google Analytics load once, through GTM only?

Your call7. Home page message

The hero line in the mock is "Test your Microsoft 365 security, every day, in one run." maester.cloud leads with "Know what changed". Does this split, where maester.dev is about testing and Cloud about change, match how you want to position the two?

Recommend: video, live player if it tests well8. Explainers: video or live HTML

Embed rendered video (works everywhere, can also go on YouTube), or play the HyperFrames HTML live with its player component (sharper, lighter, follows the theme). Should the explainers have a voice-over, or captions only?

# Maester Test Report

This folder contains the test report for the Maester project.

Vite and `vite-plugin-singlefile` generate the self-contained HTML template used by
`Get-MtHtmlReport`. The production bundle uses Preact's React-compatible runtime.

## Developer guide

### Pre-requisites

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/) version 20.0 or above (which can be checked by running `node -v`). You can use [nvm](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm) for managing multiple Node versions on a single machine installed.
- When installing Node.js, you are recommended to check all checkboxes related to dependencies.

### First time run

Open terminal window and navigate to /report folder and run the following command to install all dependencies:

```shell
npm install
```

### Development

To start the development server, run the following command:

```shell
npm run dev
```

### Build

Once you are done with making updates to the report, you can build the project to create the .html template and copy it over to the /powershell folder.

To build the project, run the following command:

```shell
npm run build
```

Before any of this goes live we need written approval from Audrey for each quote and clip, and from Microsoft for using the Xbox name. If Microsoft won't approve the brand, the same section works as "a Microsoft gaming security team" with the episode link.

    1. Clips cut in Riverside. The episodes are already recorded there. Each clip is 30 to 60 seconds, with burned-in captions in the site's type and a poster frame designed from our tokens (the dark quote card in the mock), never a raw video still.

    Stable and preview

    Maester ships on two channels. Every push to main that touches the module publishes a preview to the PowerShell Gallery (publish-module-preview.yaml), and a stable release comes out every few weeks. So at any moment a new check or parameter can exist in the preview while most people run stable. Separately, a check inside a stable release can be marked preview and only run with -IncludePreview. The docs need to be right for all three cases without copying themselves.

    Today we solve this the Docusaurus way: a full copy of the docs per version (/docs for 2.3.0, /docs/next for 3.0). That copy is what created our 1,033 duplicate pages, and it means a fix has to be made twice. The redesign keeps one page per thing and marks versions inside it. The Docs versions board shows it working, with a switch for a reader on stable or on preview.

    Where the version facts come from

    • Two catalogs. The module build already writes a test catalog with CatalogVersion. The site build reads the catalog and command help of the latest stable and the latest preview module (from their GitHub releases or the Gallery packages) and compares them: what's only in preview, what changed, what was retired.
    • A history file. Each release appends the test IDs, commands and parameters it contains to website/data/versions.json, so every item has an "Added in" version. We seed it once from past releases.
    • The two current versions. website/version-config.js, which the publish workflows already update, says which version is stable and which is the preview.

    What a reader sees

    PageReader on stableReader on preview
    A check only in the previewA banner: in the 3.1 preview, not in your version yet, with Install-Module Maester -AllowPrerelease"Added in 3.1.0-preview" under the title
    A check marked preview in a release"Preview check: runs with -IncludePreview" on its page and in the catalogSame
    A check whose logic changed in previewThe stable guidance, plus "The 3.1 preview changes this check" with the differenceThe new guidance, with "Changed in 3.1"
    Command parametersStable syntax; new parameters marked Preview 3.1, removed ones markedPreview syntax; new parameters marked New in 3.1
    GuidesPreview-only sections marked and collapsedEverything open, with "New in 3.1" marks
    Test catalogStable checks; a switch adds preview-only checksEvery check in the preview

    The reader picks their channel once in the header. The choice is remembered on their device. Links from the HTML report and the console carry the version that produced them (?v=3.0.4), so a check's page can say "added in 3.0.6; update to get it" to someone on an older patch. The version is never part of the path, so there is still exactly one URL per check and per command for search engines. Preview-only pages are indexed too: they become stable within weeks, and indexing early gives them a head start.

    How writers mark versions

    • Docs change in the same pull request as the code. A section that only applies from the next release goes in <Since version="3.1">; a change in behaviour goes in <Changed in="3.1">, which says what it was before. A new page sets since: 3.1 in its front matter.
    • Writers never edit the label. The build compares the version with version-config.js: above stable, it shows Preview 3.1; once 3.1 is stable, New in 3.1; two minor releases later the mark disappears on its own. Nothing to clean up after a release.
    • Generated pages (checks and commands) need no marks at all: the catalogs and the history file give the versions.
    • A lint step fails the build for a version that is neither the current stable nor the upcoming one, which catches typos such as since="31".

    Majors and patches

    Patch releases get no docs of their own; "Added in 3.0.6" covers them. A major release that breaks things (2.x to 3.0, later 3.x to 4.0) freezes the old major as a static, noindex archive (/docs/2.x/, later /docs/3.x/), linked from its upgrade guide. input.recap: The proposal now covers stable and preview docs (one page per item, with version marks) and how explainers stay current. A new interactive Docs versions board shows both. Still a proposal; nothing in the repository has changed.

content.text:
Short answer: keep a single set of docs for both channels, and mark inside each page which release added what. That's simpler than copying the docs for each version, which is how we got `/docs/next` and its 1,033 duplicate pages.

The proposal has a new section, "Stable and preview": https://claude.ai/artifact/7BUFL5w1kw6PMLNLKsTVZ8. The mocks have a new interactive board, "Docs versions: stable and preview": https://claude.ai/artifact/PfMudyAzivfxvRSrHibqiT. It has a switch to view the pages as a reader on stable or as a reader on preview. I couldn't view it in the browser pane because it isn't signed in, so I checked the markup and the switch logic with a script instead.

**Three version cases to handle.** Every push to main that changes the module already publishes a preview to the PowerShell Gallery, and stable releases come out on their own schedule. That gives three cases:
- **Only in the preview:** a check or parameter that exists in the preview but not in stable yet.
- **Changed in the preview:** a check or command that behaves differently in the preview.
- **Preview check:** a check that ships in a stable release but only runs with `-IncludePreview`.

**Where the version facts come from:**
- **Module catalogs:** the module build already writes a test catalog. The site build reads the catalog and command help from both the latest stable and the latest preview module, and compares them.
- **History file:** each release adds its test IDs, commands and parameters to `website/data/versions.json`, so every item has an "Added in" version.
- **Current versions:** the publish workflows already keep `website/version-config.js` up to date with which version is stable and which is the preview.

**What readers see:**
- **Version picker:** readers choose stable or preview once, in the header, and it's remembered on their device.
- **A check only in the preview:** someone on stable sees a banner saying it isn't in their version yet, with the `Install-Module Maester -AllowPrerelease` command.
- **Command pages:** stable syntax by default. Parameters only in the preview are marked "Preview 3.1"; once that release is stable, the mark becomes "New in 3.1".
- **Links from the report:** they carry the version that ran (`?v=3.0.4`), so the page can say "added in 3.0.6, update to get it".
- **URLs:** the version never goes in the path, so there's still one URL per check and per command.

**How writers mark versions:**
- **Same PR as the code:** docs change in the pull request that changes the code.
- **Tags:** a section that applies from the next release goes in `<Since version="3.1">`, and a behaviour change goes in `<Changed in="3.1">`.
- **Labels change on their own:** the build compares the tag with `version-config.js`. It shows "Preview" before the release, "New in 3.1" after it, and drops the mark two minor releases later, so there's nothing to clean up.
- **Generated pages:** test and command pages need no tags at all.
- **Majors and patches:** each major version becomes a frozen archive, like `/docs/2.x/`, and patch releases get no docs of their own.
- **next.maester.dev is dropped:** I'd suggested it earlier as a separate preview site, but it's no longer needed. Reviewers use the preview deployment Cloudflare builds for each pull request.

**Keeping the HyperFrames explainers current:**
- **Data-driven:** explainers read their numbers, gate names, reason codes and command syntax from the same data as the docs, so a release updates them on the next render.
- **Watch list:** each explainer lists the source files it describes. A pull request that touches one gets a reminder from maester-bot naming the explainer to check. It reminds; it doesn't block the merge.
- **Version tags:** chapters can carry `since` the same way guide sections do.
- **Every render kept:** docs pages show the latest, and a blog post can stay on the version it was written with.
- **Agent skill:** a `maester-explainers` skill lets Claude Code update an explainer as part of the feature's pull request.

This changes my recommendation on the format decision (number 8). Use the live HyperFrames player on the site, because a merged change goes live with the next deploy and there's no video to re-render. Make rendered videos only for YouTube, social posts, and browsers that can't run the player.

PowerShell 7.6.2
<#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Exports the built-in Maester test catalog to JSON for the website test-docs generator.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Imports the Maester module from source (powershell/Maester.psd1), reads every built-in native test
    with Get-MtTest and writes its metadata to a JSON file. website/scripts/generate-test-docs.mjs reads
    that file, plus each test's Test.<ID>.md, to build the pages in website/docs/tests/.

    Each test has its attributes (Product, RelatedProduct, Feature, Area and ResourceType as taxonomy keys),
    the derived Block, Suite and Source, and LegacyTag: the tags it carried in Maester 2.x, which -Tag still
    matches. Taxonomy at the top level gives the display names of the keys and ATT&CK techniques the tests use.

    A test of a suite that implements a published benchmark also has Benchmark, from the framework file of its
    suite (tests/<suite>/frameworks/<key>.json): Framework, Version, Requirement and the requirement's own
    facts, such as the CIS level and profiles. Its Control lists the controls of other frameworks that the
    requirement relates to. Benchmark is null for every other test. Frameworks at the top level gives the Name,
    Version and Url of each framework by Key.

    No tenant connection is needed and no test code is run. Importing the module requires
    Microsoft.Graph.Authentication to be installed (it is a RequiredModule of Maester).

    The output is deterministic: tests are sorted by ID (ordinal, case-insensitive), paths are
    repository-relative with forward slashes, and the file is UTF-8 without BOM with LF line endings.

    .PARAMETER OutputPath
    Where to write the JSON file. Defaults to website/.generated/test-catalog.json (git-ignored).

    .EXAMPLE
    ./build/docs/Export-MtTestCatalogForDocs.ps1

    Writes website/.generated/test-catalog.json, then `npm run generate-test-docs` (in website/) uses it.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [Parameter()]
    [string] $OutputPath
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

## SYNOPSIS

This is the main Maester command that runs the tests and generates a report of the results.

## SYNTAX

```powershell
Invoke-Maester [[-Path] <String>] [-Tag <String[]>] [-ExcludeTag <String[]>] [-Product <String[]>]
 [-ExcludeProduct <String[]>] [-Feature <String[]>] [-Area <String[]>] [-Severity <String[]>]
 [-Suite <String[]>] [-Pack <String[]>] [-AllPacks] [-IncludeLongRunning] [-IncludePreview]
 [-OutputHtmlFile <String>] [-IncludeAffectedObjects] [-RedactUserIdentity <String>]
 [-OutputMarkdownFile <String>] [-OutputMarkdownSummaryFile <String>] [-OutputJsonFile <String>]
 [-OutputFolder <String>] [-OutputFolderFileName <String>] [-PesterConfiguration <Object>]
 [-Verbosity <String>] [-NonInteractive] [-PassThru] [-MailRecipient <String[]>] [-MailTestResultsUri <String>]
 [-MailUserId <String>] [-TeamId <String>] [-TeamChannelId <String>] [-TeamChannelWebhookUri <String>]
 [-SkipGraphConnect] [-DisableTelemetry] [-SkipVersionCheck] [-ExportCsv] [-ExportExcel] [-NoLogo]
 [-OutputMode <String>] [-DriftRoot <String>] [-TestId <String[]>] [-ExcludeTestId <String[]>]
 [-Config <Object>] [-DryRun] [-SkipBuiltIn] [-PackLock <String>] [-SkipPack]
 [-ProgressAction <ActionPreference>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

Using Invoke-Maester is the easiest way to run the Pester tests and generate a report of the results.

For more advanced configuration, you can directly use the Pester module and the Get-MtHtmlReport function.

By default, Invoke-Maester runs the tests that ship with Maester and the custom tests in the Custom folder of the current directory, except Active Directory tests, preview tests and long-running tests.
With -Path, native custom tests (Test.*.ps1) are found anywhere under the path and Pester-format custom tests (*.Tests.ps1) only in a Custom folder.
Folders are searched up to three levels deep.

import { z } from 'astro/zod'

import { blogAuthorSchema } from '../schema'

import { throwPluginError } from './error'
import { stripLeadingSlash, stripTrailingSlash } from './path'

const blogConfigSchema = z
  .object({
    authors: z.record(z.string(), blogAuthorSchema).default({}),
    metrics: z
      .object({
        readingTime: z.boolean().default(false),
        words: z.union([z.literal(false), z.literal('total'), z.literal('rounded')]).default(false),
      })
      .default({ readingTime: false, words: false }),
    navigation: z.union([z.literal('header-start'), z.literal('header-end'), z.literal('none')]).default('header-end'),
    prefix: z
      .string()
      .default('blog')
      .transform((value) => stripTrailingSlash(stripLeadingSlash(value))),
    prevNextLinksOrder: z
      .union([z.literal('chronological'), z.literal('reverse-chronological')])
      .default('reverse-chronological'),
    postCount: z
      .union([z.number().min(1), z.literal(Infinity)])
      .default(5)
      .transform(infinityToMax),
    recentPostCount: z
      .union([z.number().min(1), z.literal(Infinity)])
      .default(10)
      .transform(infinityToMax),
    rss: z.boolean().default(true),
    structuredData: z.boolean().default(true),
    title: z.union([z.string(), z.record(z.string(), z.string())]).default('Blog'),
  })
  .prefault({})

---
title: Installation guide
---

Maester needs **PowerShell 7.4 or later** on Windows, Linux or macOS. Windows PowerShell 5.1 is not supported.

- Install the **Maester** PowerShell module.

```powershell
Install-Module Maester -Scope CurrentUser
```

The tests ship inside the module, so there is nothing else to download and no folder to set up.

- Sign into your Microsoft 365 tenant and run the tests.

```powershell
Connect-Maester
Invoke-Maester
```

You only need a folder if you want to change settings or add your own tests. Put a `maester-config.json` (see [Configuration](configuration/overview.md)) and a `custom` folder for your tests (see [Writing custom tests](writing-tests/index.mdx)) in it, and run `Invoke-Maester -Path <folder>` or run Maester from that folder.

:::note[Pester]
Maester 3.0 does not need Pester. Install it only if you have custom tests written in the Pester format (`*.Tests.ps1`), see [Pester-format tests](writing-tests/pester-format-tests.md):

```powershell
Install-Module Pester -MinimumVersion 5.7.1 -SkipPublisherCheck -Force -Scope CurrentUser
```
:::

---
title: Get the preview
description: How to install the Maester preview to use checks and commands that aren't in the stable release yet, how to use it in your pipelines, and how to go back to the stable release.
sidebar:
  label: Get the preview
  order: 3
---

Maester ships on two channels:

- **Stable** releases come out every few weeks. Most people, and most pipelines, should run stable.
- A **preview** is published to the PowerShell Gallery every time a change is merged. It has every new check, command and option as soon as it is merged, before the next stable release.

These docs describe the preview. A check, command or parameter that the stable release doesn't have yet is marked **Preview** on its page and in the [test catalog](/docs/tests). Pick the version you run from the version menu at the top of the page, and the marks say what your version doesn't have.

## Install the preview

```powershell
Install-Module Maester -AllowPrerelease -Force -Scope CurrentUser
```

Check which version PowerShell loads:

```powershell
Get-Module Maester -ListAvailable | Select-Object Name, Version, PrivateData
Import-Module Maester -Force
Get-Module Maester
```

A preview version ends in `-preview` followed by a number, for example `3.1.0-preview04`.

If you use PSResourceGet instead of PowerShellGet:

```powershell
Install-PSResource Maester -Prerelease -Reinstall
```

## Use the preview in automation {#github-actions}

**GitHub Actions.** Set `maester_version` to `preview` in the Maester action:

```yaml
- uses: maester365/maester-action@main
  with:
    tenant_id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
    client_id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
    maester_major_version: "3"
    maester_version: preview
```

**Azure DevOps, Azure Automation and other pipelines.** Install the module with `-AllowPrerelease`:

```powershell
Install-Module Maester -AllowPrerelease -Force -Scope CurrentUser
```

The preview changes with every merge. For a pipeline other people rely on, run the preview in a second, non-blocking job next to your stable job, or pin an exact preview version with `-RequiredVersion 3.1.0-preview04 -AllowPrerelease`.

## Go back to the stable release

```powershell
Uninstall-Module Maester -AllVersions -AllowPrerelease -Force
Install-Module Maester -Force -Scope CurrentUser
```

In GitHub Actions, set `maester_version` back to `latest`.

## Preview releases and preview checks

Two different things are called preview:

- **The preview release** is the module version described on this page. Install it with `-AllowPrerelease`.
- **A preview check** is a check that is still being tested or depends on a preview Microsoft API. It ships in any release, stable or preview, but only runs when you add `-IncludePreview` to `Invoke-Maester`. Its page says so.

## Tell us what you find

The preview is how new checks get tested on real tenants before they reach everyone. If something fails or reads wrong, open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues) or ask in [Discord](https://discord.maester.dev).

# @hyperframes/player

Embeddable web component for playing HyperFrames compositions. Zero dependencies, works with any framework.

## Install

```bash
npm install @hyperframes/player
```

Or load directly via CDN:

```html
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@hyperframes/player"></script>
```

If you need a classic `<script>` tag instead of ESM, use the explicit global build:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@hyperframes/player/dist/hyperframes-player.global.js"></script>
```

## Usage

```html
<hyperframes-player src="./my-composition/index.html" controls></hyperframes-player>
```

The player loads the composition in a sandboxed iframe, auto-detects its dimensions and duration, and scales it responsively to fit the container.

### With a framework

```typescript
import "@hyperframes/player";

// The custom element is now registered — use it in your markup
// React: <hyperframes-player src="..." controls />
// Vue:   <hyperframes-player :src="url" controls />
```

### Poster image

Show a static image before playback starts:

```html
<hyperframes-player
  src="./composition/index.html"
  poster="./thumbnail.jpg"
  controls
></hyperframes-player>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute              | Type                            | Default       | Description                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src`                  | string                          | —             | URL to the composition HTML file                                            |
| `audio-src`            | string                          | —             | Audio URL for parent-frame playback (mobile)                                |
| `width`                | number                          | 1920          | Composition width in pixels (aspect ratio)                                  |
| `height`               | number                          | 1080          | Composition height in pixels (aspect ratio)                                 |
| `controls`             | boolean                         | false         | Show play/pause, scrubber, and time display                                 |
| `muted`                | boolean                         | false         | Mute audio playback                                                         |
| `audio-locked`         | boolean                         | false         | Force-mute and hide the volume controls so the viewer cannot turn sound on  |
| `poster`               | string                          | —             | Image URL shown before playback starts                                      |
| `playback-rate`        | number                          | 1             | Speed multiplier (0.5 = half, 2 = double)                                   |
| `autoplay`             | boolean                         | false         | Start playing when ready                                                    |
| `loop`                 | boolean                         | false         | Restart when the composition ends                                           |
| `shader-capture-scale` | number                          | —             | Shader transition snapshot scale forwarded to browser previews (`0.25`-`1`) |
| `shader-loading`       | `composition \| player \| none` | `composition` | Controls shader transition prep loading UI ownership                        |

### Shader transition previews

When a composition uses `@hyperframes/shader-transitions`, the player can own preview-only shader capture settings:

```html
<hyperframes-player
  src="./composition/index.html"
  shader-capture-scale="1"
  shader-loading="player"
  controls
></hyperframes-player>
```

`shader-loading="player"` shows the player-owned transition-prep overlay from shader progress messages. `composition` leaves direct composition fallback behavior alone, and `none` suppresses the loader.

### Audio lock (host-mandated silent playback)

`audio-locked` forces `muted` on and hides the volume controls, with no UI path for the viewer to turn sound back on. Use it when embedding in a chat host (Claude.ai, ChatGPT, etc.) where audio must stay off regardless of viewer intent. Setting `muted` directly is _not_ enough — viewers can flip it back via the controls bar.

Removing `audio-locked` only unhides the controls; it does **not** auto-unmute. Callers manage `muted` explicitly after unlocking.

**Host-environment fallback.** Some host renderers — notably the Claude desktop Electron client — strip unknown custom-element attributes before they reach the DOM, defeating the attribute. As a safety net, the player also self-imposes the lock when it detects such an environment via `navigator.userAgent`, so audio stays muted even if the attribute never arrives. The public `audioLocked` property still reflects only the attribute, so external consumers (e.g. host widgets that mirror state) are not affected by the fallback.

### Mobile audio

Mobile browsers block `audio.play()` inside iframes when the user gesture happened in the parent frame (the [User Activation spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#tracking-user-activation) does not propagate activation across frame boundaries via `postMessage`).

The player handles this automatically for same-origin iframes (the default — `sandbox` includes `allow-same-origin`):

1. When the composition is ready, the player extracts all timed media (`audio[data-start]`, `video[data-start]`) from the iframe DOM and creates parent-frame copies.
2. The iframe originals are disabled (`src` and `data-start` removed) so the runtime doesn't try to play them.
3. When `play()` is called (from a user gesture), parent media `.play()` runs synchronously in the gesture call stack, satisfying mobile autoplay policy.
4. Both parent media and the GSAP timeline start simultaneously and free-run — no active sync needed since both are real-time systems.

No changes are required by consumers — this works out of the box.

The optional `audio-src` attribute can be used to start preloading a primary audio track before the iframe loads (useful on slow connections), but is not required for mobile playback.

## JavaScript API

```js
const player = document.querySelector("hyperframes-player");

// Playback
player.play();
player.pause();
player.seek(2.5); // jump to 2.5 seconds

// Properties
player.currentTime; // number (read/write)

# Data Attributes

Core attributes for controlling element timing and behavior.

## Timing

- `data-start="0"` — Start time in seconds
- `data-duration="5"` — Duration in seconds
- `data-track-index="0"` — Timeline track number (controls z-ordering)

## Media

- `data-media-start="2"` — Media playback offset / trim point (seconds)
- `data-volume="0.8"` — Audio/video volume, 0 to 1
- `data-has-audio="true"` — Indicates video has an audio track

## Composition

- `data-composition-id="root"` — Unique ID for composition wrapper (required)
- `data-width="1920"` — Composition width in pixels
- `data-height="1080"` — Composition height in pixels
- `data-composition-src="./intro.html"` — Nested composition source

## Element Visibility

Add `class="clip"` to timed elements so the runtime can manage their visibility lifecycle.
# GSAP Animation

HyperFrames uses GSAP for animation. Timelines are paused and controlled by the runtime.

## Setup

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3/dist/gsap.min.js"></script>
<script>
  const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
  tl.to("#title", { opacity: 1, duration: 0.5 }, 0);
  window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
  window.__timelines["root"] = tl;
</script>
```

## Key Rules

- Always create timelines with `{ paused: true }`
- Register timelines on `window.__timelines` with the composition ID as key
- Position parameter (3rd arg) sets absolute time: `tl.to(el, vars, 1.5)`
- Supported methods: `set`, `to`, `from`, `fromTo`

## Supported Properties

opacity, x, y, scale, scaleX, scaleY, rotation, width, height, visibility

# Validates that the Docusaurus website builds successfully.
# Runs on PRs that modify website files or docs source files, and can also be
# called from other workflows or triggered manually.
name: "\U0001F3D7️ Build Website"

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      node_version:
        description: "Node.js version to use."
        required: false
        default: "24.x"
        type: string
      working_directory:
        description: "Path to the directory containing package.json (relative to the repository root)."
        required: false
        default: "website"
        type: string
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
    branches: ["main"]
    paths:
      - "build/Update-CommandReference.ps1"
      - "build/eidsca/*.json"
      - "powershell/**"
      - "tests/**"
      - "website/**"
      - ".github/workflows/build-website.yaml"

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  detect-command-reference-changes:
    name: "Detect command reference changes"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      generate: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || steps.filter.outputs.command_reference == 'true' }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Check command reference inputs
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        id: filter
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@ceb8a2b8f2d89434be7ff52d3de7ec3738c5cc9d # v4.0.3
        with:
          filters: |
            command_reference:
              - "build/Update-CommandReference.ps1"
              - "powershell/**"
              - "tests/**"
              - ".github/workflows/build-website.yaml"

  generate-command-reference:
    name: "Generate command reference"
    needs: detect-command-reference-changes
    if: needs.detect-command-reference-changes.outputs.generate == 'true'
    runs-on: windows-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Generate command reference
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./build/Update-CommandReference.ps1

      - name: Package generated command reference
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ProgressPreference = "SilentlyContinue"
          $artifactRoot = Join-Path $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE "generated-command-reference"
          $docsRoot = Join-Path $artifactRoot "docs"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $docsRoot -Force | Out-Null

          $sourceCommands = Join-Path $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE "website/docs/commands"
          if (-not (Test-Path $sourceCommands)) {
            throw "Command reference docs were not generated at $sourceCommands."
          }

          Copy-Item -Path $sourceCommands -Destination $docsRoot -Recurse -Force

          $versionedDocsRoot = Join-Path $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE "website/versioned_docs"
          if (Test-Path $versionedDocsRoot) {
            foreach ($versionFolder in Get-ChildItem $versionedDocsRoot -Directory) {
              $sourceVersionCommands = Join-Path $versionFolder.FullName "commands"
              if (Test-Path $sourceVersionCommands) {
                $targetVersionRoot = Join-Path $artifactRoot "versioned_docs/$($versionFolder.Name)"
                New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $targetVersionRoot -Force | Out-Null
                Copy-Item -Path $sourceVersionCommands -Destination $targetVersionRoot -Recurse -Force
              }
            }
          }

          Compress-Archive -Path (Join-Path $artifactRoot "*") -DestinationPath command-reference-docs.zip -Force

      - name: Upload generated command reference
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: generated-command-reference
          path: command-reference-docs.zip
          if-no-files-found: error

  build:
    name: "Build Docusaurus website \U0001F3D7️"
    needs: [detect-command-reference-changes, generate-command-reference]
    if: always() && needs.detect-command-reference-changes.result == 'success' && (needs.generate-command-reference.result == 'success' || needs.generate-command-reference.result == 'skipped')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: ⬇️ Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Full history so contributor profiles get display names and first-contribution dates from git.
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Download generated command reference
        if: needs.detect-command-reference-changes.outputs.generate == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: generated-command-reference
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/command-reference

      - name: Apply generated command reference
        if: needs.detect-command-reference-changes.outputs.generate == 'true'
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          WEBSITE_WORKING_DIRECTORY: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}
        run: |
          $ProgressPreference = "SilentlyContinue"
          Remove-Item -Path (Join-Path $env:WEBSITE_WORKING_DIRECTORY "docs/commands") -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

          $versionedDocsRoot = Join-Path $env:WEBSITE_WORKING_DIRECTORY "versioned_docs"
          if (Test-Path $versionedDocsRoot) {
            foreach ($versionFolder in Get-ChildItem $versionedDocsRoot -Directory) {
              Remove-Item -Path (Join-Path $versionFolder.FullName "commands") -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            }
          }

          Expand-Archive -Path "${{ runner.temp }}/command-reference/command-reference-docs.zip" -DestinationPath $env:WEBSITE_WORKING_DIRECTORY -Force

      - name: ⚙️ Set up Node.js ${{ inputs.node_version || '24.x' }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node_version || '24.x' }}
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}/package-lock.json

      - name: "\U0001F4E6 Install dependencies"
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}
        run: npm ci

      # The test docs are generated from the source module (Get-MtTest), which needs this module to import.
      # Without it the generator keeps the committed pages, so a PR's new or changed tests would not render.
      - name: Install Microsoft.Graph.Authentication for the test docs generator
        shell: pwsh
        run: Install-Module Microsoft.Graph.Authentication -MinimumVersion 2.27.0 -Scope CurrentUser -Repository PSGallery -Force

      - name: "\U0001F3D7️ Build website"
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}
        env:
          # Lets the contributor generator resolve new commit emails to GitHub
          # handles (cached in website/contributors/email-aliases.json).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: npm run build

        shell: pwsh

      - name: Package generated command reference
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ProgressPreference = "SilentlyContinue"
          $artifactRoot = Join-Path $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE "generated-command-reference"
          $docsRoot = Join-Path $artifactRoot "docs"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $docsRoot -Force | Out-Null

          $sourceCommands = Join-Path $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE "website/docs/commands"
          if (-not (Test-Path $sourceCommands)) {
            throw "Command reference docs were not generated at $sourceCommands."
          }

          Copy-Item -Path $sourceCommands -Destination $docsRoot -Recurse -Force

          Compress-Archive -Path (Join-Path $artifactRoot "*") -DestinationPath command-reference-docs.zip -Force

      - name: Upload generated command reference

## Contributing to Maester docs and blog posts

Simple edits can be made in the GitHub UI by selecting the `Edit this page` link at the bottom of each page or you can browse to the [docs](https://github.com/maester365/maester/tree/main/website/docs) folder on GitHub.

For more complex changes, you can fork the repository and submit a pull request.

The docs/commands folder is auto-generated based on the comments in the PowerShell cmdlets. If you want to update the documentation for a command, you will need to update the comment-based help in the .ps1 file for the command.

### Running documentation locally

The [Maester.dev](https://maester.dev) website is built using [Docusaurus](https://docusaurus.io/).

Follow this guide if you want to run the documentation locally and view changes in real-time.

#### Pre-requisites

[Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/) version 24.0 or above (which can be checked by running node -v). When installing Node.js, you are recommended to check all checkboxes related to dependencies.

#### Installation

When running the documentation for the first time, you will need to install the dependencies. This can be done by running the following command in ./website folder.

```shell
npm install
```

#### Starting the site

While in the ./website folder, run the following command to start the site locally. This will start a local server and open the site in your default browser to [http://localhost:3000/](http://localhost:3000/)

```shell
npm start
```

#### Editing content

You will now be able to edit add and edit markdown files in the ./website/docs folder and see the changes in real-time in your browser.

- Read the [markdown documentation](https://docusaurus.io/docs/markdown-features) for more information on some of the custom markdown features available.
- You can search for icons at [Iconify](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/) and include them in the markdown. See the [Daily Automation](https://maester.dev/docs/automation/) page for examples.
- The `Command Reference` section is auto-generated. To update the documentation for this, the .ps1 file for the command needs to be updated with comment-based documentation.

#### Blog post images

Every blog post has a card image (`img/card.png` in the post's folder) that is shown on the [blog](https://maester.dev/blog) and in link previews on social media. The images all use one template, so don't make one by hand.

The [Maester.dev](https://maester.dev) website is built with [Astro](https://astro.build) and [Starlight](https://starlight.astro.build).

#### Pre-requisites

[Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/) 22.22 or later (`node -v`). The CI builds use Node.js 24.

#### Installation

In the `./website` folder, install the dependencies:

```shell
npm install
```

#### Starting the site

While in the `./website` folder, start the site. It runs at [http://localhost:4321/](http://localhost:4321/) and reloads as you edit:

```shell
npm start
```

`npm run build` builds the whole site into `website/dist` and then checks that every URL the site has ever had still works (see [URLs](#urls) below).

#### Editing content

Guides are Markdown files in `./website/docs`. A file's path is its URL: `docs/monitoring/github.md` is
`https://maester.dev/docs/monitoring/github`, and a `readme.md` or `index.md` is its folder's page.

- Link to other pages by their file, such as `[Configuration](configuration/overview.md)`. The site turns these
  links into URLs, and they also work when you read the docs on GitHub.
- Notes and warnings use Starlight's syntax: `:::note`, `:::tip`, `:::caution` or `:::danger`, with an optional
  title in brackets (`:::tip[Before you start]`).
- A page that uses components (tabs, icons, explainers) is an `.mdx` file and imports them, for example
  `import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';` or
  `import IIcon from '@components/IIcon.astro';` for an [Iconify](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/) icon. See
  [Starlight's components](https://starlight.astro.build/components/using-components/).
- The pages under `Commands` are generated from each command's comment-based help: edit the `.ps1` file, not the page.
- The test pages are built from each test's `[MaesterTest]` attribute and `Test.<ID>.md`: edit those, not the
  website. `npm run export-catalog` refreshes `website/src/data/test-catalog.json` from your local tests (it needs
  PowerShell 7 and the `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication` module).

#### Stable and preview

The docs describe the preview, which is published to the PowerShell Gallery each time a change is merged. Checks,
commands and parameters that the stable release doesn't have are marked **Preview** automatically, from the test
catalog and `website/src/data/versions.json`; you don't mark them yourself.

In a guide, wrap a section that only applies from the next release in `<Since version="3.1">`, or describe a change
in behaviour with `<Changed in="3.1">` (both from `@components/Since.astro`). The build compares the version with
`website/version-config.js` and shows **Preview 3.1** or **New in 3.1**; the release workflows keep both files up to
date. Write the docs in the same pull request as the change.

#### Explainers

Short animated explainers (in the intro and the applicability guide, and on the home page) are
[HyperFrames](https://hyperframes.heygen.com) compositions: HTML and CSS with a GSAP timeline, in
`website/public/explainers/<name>/index.html`. Their chapters and transcript are in `website/src/data/explainers.json`;
keep the two in step. Preview one with `npx hyperframes preview` in its folder. Each composition lists the source
files it describes (`Watches:` in its header comment). If your change alters what an explainer shows, such as a gate,
a reason code or a command's output, update the explainer in the same pull request.

#### URLs

`website/src/data/url-contract.txt` lists every URL the site had when it moved to Astro, and `npm run build` fails if
any of them no longer opens a page, directly or through a redirect in `website/src/lib/redirects.mjs`. When you move or
rename a page, add a redirect from its old URL.

### Site versioning

There are two versions of the Maester website:

- [Production](https://maester.dev) - This is the live version of the site that is updated whenever a new version of the Maester module is released.
- [Preview](https://preview.maester.dev) - This is the version of the site that is updated with every commit to the main branch. This allows you to see changes before they are published to production.

| Environment | URL | Branch | Update Trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Production | [https://maester.dev](https://maester.dev) | website-prod | New Maester module release |
| Preview | [https://preview.maester.dev](https://preview.maester.dev) | main | Every commit to the main branch |

When a new version of the Maester module is released, the documentation will be updated to reflect the changes in that version.

#### Version numbers

A preview is a prerelease of the release it leads to, and the docs show that release's number.

| | Module on the PowerShell Gallery | Shown on the preview site |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Previews of 3.0 | `3.0.0-preview1` to `3.0.0-preview9`, then `3.0.0-rc01`, `3.0.0-rc02`, ... | `3.0.0-preview` |
| The release | `3.0.0` | `3.0.0` |
| Previews after it | `3.1.0-preview01`, `3.1.0-preview02`, ... | `3.1.0-preview` |

- A preview never uses up a release number, and every preview sorts below its release, so people on a preview are
  offered the release.
- The PowerShell Gallery compares prerelease labels as text, so the preview number has two digits: `preview10`
  sorts above `preview09` but below `preview9`. That is why the 3.0 previews after `preview9` are `rc01` and on.
- The numbers are worked out by `.github/workflows/Get-NextModuleVersion.ps1` from what is on the gallery. To start
  a new major version, raise `$major` in `.github/workflows/minor-version-update.ps1`.
- PowerShell installs `3.0.0-preview2` and `3.0.0` into the same folder. Someone who has a preview moves to the
  release with `Install-Module Maester -Force`; Maester tells them so when it starts.

#### Urgent changes to blog posts and documentation

If a blog post or doc change is urgent and cannot wait till the next release, create a PR against the `website-prod` branch directly.

Once that is reviewed and merged, you will need to create another PR to bring the changes into the `main` branch.

This is because the `website-prod` branch is deleted and recreated with every Maester module release to ensure it is always in sync with the released version of the module.

This process ensures any interim changes to the production site are intentional.

cd /Users/merill/github/maester/.claude/worktrees/website-astro/website; cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# maester.dev

The Maester website: the home page, the docs, the test catalog, the command reference and the blog. It is built with
[Astro](https://astro.build) and [Starlight](https://starlight.astro.build), and shares its design tokens with
[maester.cloud](https://maester.cloud).

```shell
npm install
npm start          # http://localhost:4321
npm run build      # builds dist/, then checks that every old URL still resolves
```

Node.js 22.22 or later. The contributing guide has the details: [Contributing to Maester docs](https://maester.dev/docs/contributing#contributing-to-maester-docs-and-blog-posts).

## Where things are

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/` | The guides and the command reference (`docs/commands`, generated by `build/Update-CommandReference.ps1`). A file's path is its URL. |
| `blog/` | Blog posts, one folder each. |
| `versioned_docs/version-2.3.0/` | The Maester 2.x docs, frozen, served at `/docs/2.x` with `noindex`. |
| `src/data/test-catalog.json` | Every built-in test, exported by `npm run export-catalog`. The test pages and the catalog are built from it at build time by `scripts/generate-test-docs.mjs` (into the ignored `.generated/`). |
| `src/data/versions.json` | The release each test, command and parameter first shipped in. With `version-config.js` it decides what is marked **Preview**. |
| `src/data/url-contract.txt` | Every URL the site had before the move to Astro. The build fails if one stops resolving. |
| `src/lib/redirects.mjs` | Writes `dist/_redirects` (Cloudflare Pages) for the URLs that moved. |
| `src/lib/content-loader.ts` | Loads the guides, tests, 2.x archive and blog into Starlight with the URLs they had on Docusaurus. |
| `src/components/` | Starlight overrides (`overrides/`), the version picker, the test catalog, the explainer player and the other components. |
| `src/pages/` | The pages outside the docs: home, sponsor, contributors, manifesto, test builder, EIDSCA sync. |
| `public/explainers/` | The HyperFrames explainers: HTML and GSAP, played live by `<Explainer>`. |

## Deployment

Cloudflare Pages builds the site from `main`: root directory `website`, build command `npm run build`, output
directory `dist`, Node.js 24. Pages serves `docs/intro.html` at `/docs/intro` and redirects `/docs/intro/` there, so
every URL has one form, without a trailing slash.
EOF
cat > ../.github/workflows/explainer-reminder.yaml <<'EOF'
# Reminds a pull request's author when it changes a file that one of the website's explainers describes.
# Each explainer in website/public/explainers lists the files it watches in website/src/data/explainers.json.
# It only comments: an explainer can be updated in a follow-up.
name: Explainer reminder

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, synchronize]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  remind:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      # The default branch's list of explainers, never the pull request's code.
      - name: Checkout explainer list
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: website/src/data/explainers.json
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Comment when a watched file changed
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          changed=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR/files" --jq '.[].filename')
          message=$(node -e '
            const explainers = require("./website/src/data/explainers.json");
            const changed = process.argv[1].split("\n").filter(Boolean);
            const hits = [];
            for (const [slug, e] of Object.entries(explainers)) {
              const files = changed.filter((f) => e.watches.some((w) => (w.endsWith("/") ? f.startsWith(w) : f === w)));
              const touched = changed.some((f) => f.startsWith(`website/public/explainers/${slug}/`));
              if (files.length && !touched) hits.push(`- **${e.title}** (\`website/public/explainers/${slug}/\`) describes ${files.map((f) => `\`${f}\``).join(", ")}`);
            }
            if (hits.length) console.log(hits.join("\n"));
          ' "$changed")
          if [ -z "$message" ]; then exit 0; fi
          marker="<!-- explainer-reminder -->"
          body="$marker
          This pull request changes files that a website explainer describes:

          $message

          If the change alters what the explainer shows (a gate, a reason code, a command, a count), update its composition and its chapters in \`website/src/data/explainers.json\`. If it doesn't, no action is needed."
          existing=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR/comments" --jq ".[] | select(.body | startswith(\"$marker\")) | .id" | head -1)
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh api -X PATCH "repos/$REPO/issues/comments/$existing" -f body="$body" > /dev/null
          else
            gh pr comment "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
          fi
EOF
echo ok

content.text:
The new maester.dev is built on Astro + Starlight. The build passes and every one of the 2,679 URLs from the old sitemap still resolves. Nothing is committed: the work is in a separate worktree, `.claude/worktrees/website-astro` on branch `feat/website-astro`, so your console branch is untouched. A local preview is running at http://localhost:4329.

**Preview by default.** The docs describe the 3.0 preview. A check or command that 2.3.0 doesn't have shows an "Only in the preview" box with `Install-Module Maester -AllowPrerelease` and links to the new [Get the preview](website/docs/preview.md) guide. That box shows whichever version the reader picks. The version picker in the header switches to "2.3.0 stable", and every mark then reads "Preview 3.0". Today that covers 192 checks, 22 commands and 16 new `Invoke-Maester` parameters. Guides can tag their own sections with `<Since version="3.1">` and `<Changed in="3.1">`.

**Keeping URLs and search ranking:**
- **No redirect hop:** every page is served at its URL without a trailing slash, matching the canonical tag and sitemap.
- **`/docs/next/*`** redirects to `/docs/*`.
- **2.3 command pages:** 659 redirect to the test that replaced them; 26 go to a frozen, noindex 2.x archive at `/docs/2.x`.
- **Build check:** `npm run build` fails if any URL in [url-contract.txt](website/src/data/url-contract.txt) stops resolving.

**What else is in it:**
- The home page from the mock: product tour, real counts, episode shelf, sponsors band with the CyberDrain and Increment logos.
- The faceted test catalog, with a copyable `Invoke-Maester` command for the current filters.
- Test pages built from one committed catalog file instead of 848 generated pages.
- Two HyperFrames explainers playing live with chapters and a transcript, plus a workflow that comments on a pull request when a change touches something an explainer describes.
- Copy page, a Markdown copy of every page, and `llms.txt`.
- The GitHub Actions, command reference generator, AGENTS.md, skills and contributing guide updated to match.

**Not done, or needs you:**
- **Cloudflare Pages settings** must change when this merges: output directory `dist` (was `build`), build command `npm run build`, Node 24. I couldn't confirm the current deploy settings from the repo.
- **The Xbox story** is in the code but hidden until you put a sign-off date in [media.json](website/src/data/media.json).
- **Also not built yet:** Sign in with ChatGPT, the docs MCP server, video renders of the explainers for YouTube, and per-page social images.
- **Repo files that still link to `/docs/next/...`** (README, pack guide) work through the redirect. I left them alone because some ship inside the module and packs.

**Tests:** 6,566 of 6,567 unit tests pass. The one failure is in the Zero Trust Assessment pack tests, and it fails the same way on a clean `main` checkout on this machine. It's not caused by this change; it looks like a side effect of version 3.1.0 of that module being installed here.

Maester 3.0 console output and performance work, done on PR 2334 (branch claude/maester-3-planning-6643a9) on 2026-10-10. Related: [[maester-3-design]].

Owner rulings (2026-10-10):
- Interactive mode prints no per-test lines at -Verbosity None, not even Failed/Error; live counts in the footer are fine "as long as it is reliable and not too many hacks".
- Keep the logo; improve it with colour for interactive runs (done: red-to-amber gradient, compact variant).
- Renderer is C# in Maester.Engine (MtConsoleRenderer).
- Perf fixes and the benchmark go in the same 3.0 PR, not separate PRs.
- Interactive runs take over the full screen with a dashboard (Copilot-CLI-style banner with the official flame, phases, product lanes, running tests); must work for future parallel runs and extra phases like data collection (as in the ZT Assessment).
- Product is a real [MaesterTest] property set on every built-in test (no parsing of Category); summary is a per-product table.
- Right-hand panels chosen by the owner: Tenant+connections, Failed by severity, Drift since last run, Pace/slowest, Blog, Version check, Tips; waffle chart of results under the lanes; user picks panels via Output.DashboardPanels. Tenant info can be absent (-SkipGraphConnect).
- CI annotations default was never ruled on; shipped on by default (cap 20, Output.CIAnnotations).

Later rulings the same day (these supersede the panel list above where they differ):
- Right column, in order: Tenant, Ring (results as a ring chart), Connections, Failed, Drift, Pace, Contributor (featured contributor), Blog, Tips. Version is not a panel: a newer version is a bold amber "↑ vX available" link under the logo.
- No extra Graph calls for the dashboard: the tenant object counts were built and then removed at the owner's request. Tenant shows name, primary domain, account only.
- Every panel should always be shown; Pace is the one that shrinks (chart + at least one test) and fills spare rows.
- Connections panel shows only which services are connected (no tenant names), connected first, alphabetical, Graph first.
- Featured contributor data is baked in at build (powershell/assets/ConsoleContributors.json via build/Update-ConsoleContributors.ps1); omit zero counts; people with pinLast are excluded.
- Status bar on the last row: wordmark gradient (owner disliked the pink/grey first version), full width, links left and right, a "⌘-click / Ctrl-click to open" hint. Owner declined mouse-tracking for one-click links after hearing the cost.
- Flame on the left of the wordmark, as on the site. No emoji in panels (terminals disagree on width).
- Layout (owner picked "option 4" after outside feedback that the logo took too much room): the big banner is only the opening screen while the run prepares; once tests start the header is one line (MAESTER in wordmark colours, version, phases). The Pace graph (one bar per test, scrolling, log scale, green-to-red rows) is in the main column between the product lanes and the result blocks. Right column in order: Tenant, Totals (stacked bar; the ring chart was tried and rejected as too blocky), Connections, Failed, Drift, Slowest (the flexible panel), Contributor, Blog, Tips.
- The owner wants mockups before layout or chart changes; show options, then build the one picked.

**Why:** the owner wants a richer TUI now that 3.0 is PowerShell 7 only, in the style of GitHub Copilot CLI.

**How to apply:** design lives in docs/proposals/maester-3.0-console-output.md; benchmark in build/perf/. Interactive runs must not use Write-Progress (its pane lands at the top of the screen in terminals that do not answer ESC[6n). The connection probe was measured at ~2.9 s (not 40 s; that was a stale Write-Progress line) and now skips EXO/Teams/PnP when their module is not imported; Azure and Azure DevOps still validate saved sign-ins over the network (~1.9 s). Open follow-ups: screen-reader detection, -DryRun still writes all reports, and (noticed 2026-10-11, not verified) the engine's "test run stopped early" error from Invoke-MtNativePlan is written while the dashboard is up and is not replayed afterwards. Warnings/errors shown after a dashboard run are only those from Write-Warning/Write-Error where the preference would show them (Get-MtDashboardMessageDefault); a default on every command replayed silenced noise such as '@odata.nextLink' cannot be found. On Windows the run switches the console to UTF-8 in Windows Terminal / VS Code only (verified by the owner on a Windows 11 VM); other Windows consoles get the ASCII fallback. My own working rule that cost me twice: read the test result before pushing, and never switch a checkout while a full suite is running in it.

**Console code review (2026-10-11):** two subagent reviews (C# renderer; PowerShell side) at 584c11d2. Fixed on PR 2334 in 58cc0497: untrusted text sanitised at the renderer boundary (PlainText / SgrOnly helpers in MtConsoleRenderer.cs; new setters must use them), hyperlinks https/file only, deferred warnings/errors after the dashboard, unknown-severity summary crash, console failures never fail a run, CI command injection in result lines, Get-Module -All in Test-MtModuleImported, terminal restore on failure and ProcessExit. Merill ruled: leave the redraw rework until the larger console changes he is bringing in; tracked with display-width measurement in maester365/maester#2361. To test the dashboard end to end without a terminal, run pwsh under a Python pty (pty.fork + TIOCSWINSZ 50x170); such runs are interactive and open the HTML report in the browser. A reviewer's full run with -SkipGraphConnect still used cached Azure and Azure DevOps sign-ins and made 48 read-only calls: use -SkipBuiltIn with a scratch custom test for no-tenant experiments.

**Design round 2026-10-18 (outlines + run progress):** Merill shared a reference video (Claude Code "opusplan tip" terminal animation) and liked its boxed panels, colours and dots running along connectors. Asked for outlines around the product lanes and running tests like the right-column panels, and an overall progress bar for the phases (Prepare, Run tests, Results, Reports). Mockups only so far, no code changed: artifact https://claude.ai/artifact/HYSY8R48JFLtGL882UbrFg (options: phases Today/Pipeline bar/Track/Boxed pipeline; outline Today/Separate boxes/One column/Coloured boxes; flow animation on/off). ## Overview
- Maester uses System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapConnection for cross-platform AD connectivity.
- TLS is required for all AD connections.
## Understanding TLS Modes
- The -ActiveDirectoryTlsMode parameter supports three values: Auto, Ldaps, StartTls.
- Auto (default): Tries LDAPS (port 636) first, then StartTLS (port 389) on Windows. On Linux/macOS, only tries LDAPS.
- Ldaps: Uses LDAPS on port 636 only.
- StartTls: Uses StartTLS on port 389 only.
- Auto mode adapts to the platform due to a known .NET limitation.
## Certificate Issues on the Domain Controller
- Common symptoms: connection fails with certificate, trust, validation, expired, or chain errors.

Two independent reviews (SEO/technical and product design) found about 50 issues; I fixed the critical and high ones and most medium ones. The site builds, all 2,679 old URLs still resolve, and the affected unit tests pass. Nothing is committed yet. You can try it in the preview at http://localhost:4329.

**Hero: the actual report.** It's the redesigned 3.0 report from your other thread, built from that worktree with its sample data, not a mock.
- There are six tabs: Overview, Action plan, A finding, Frameworks, MITRE ATT&CK and Zero Trust, each with a one-line caption.
- "Open the live report" opens the full interactive report (`/demo/report`).
- The sample data came from your demo tenant, so the build script replaces it before publishing. "Pora", elapora.com, your account and the tenant ID become Contoso. Every person's name and email becomes one of Microsoft's demo personas (Adele Vance, Megan Bowen and so on). The script refuses to write the page if any original name is left.
- This is a snapshot of uncommitted work in the other worktree. When the report changes, rerun `scripts/build-demo-report.mjs` and `scripts/capture-demo-report.mjs`.

**How it works: a 91-second narrated video.** It's a HyperFrames composition shown right under the stats, in this order:
1. A title card.
2. `Install-Module Maester`.
3. `Connect-Maester` (read-only).
4. `Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA`.
5. The console dashboard while the run goes: product lanes, running tests, Tenant, Totals, Connections, Failed and Tips.
6. The report: what to fix first, a finding, frameworks and ATT&CK, then Zero Trust.
7. An end card for running it every day.

The audio and its tooling:
- **Voice:** Kokoro (voice `af_heart`). To get the pronunciation right the script spells it "Mayster", "Microsoft three sixty-five" and "C.I.S., Sissa".
- **Music:** composed in code (a D-major progression with pad, arpeggio and bass), so there is nothing to license. It's mixed into one track and drops under the voice whenever someone is speaking.
- **Fixed a silent-audio bug:** the HyperFrames player wasn't playing audio until I self-hosted its runtime. I confirmed it with a real click: picture and sound now stay in sync.
- **Separate tools:** the voice and music tools live in `website/scripts/narration`, with a README, and CI never installs them.

**Theme toggle:** it's one button that cycles System → Light → Dark and shows the current mode. It uses three icons from your Nucleo library in the same style: the sun and moon from the Weather set, and a desktop monitor from Technology/Devices for System.

**What I fixed from the reviews:**
1. **Links:** all 36,000 internal links ended in `.html`, which costs a redirect on every click. They're now clean.
2. **Structured data:** URLs no longer end in `.html`, I added breadcrumbs, and removed a duplicate block on blog posts.
3. **Test-page descriptions:** they were 300-character raw Markdown snippets. They're now plain sentences of 155 characters or less, with no duplicates within a family of checks.
4. **Test pages:** the title is the check, without the ID and trailing period. Each page now has a "Part of" suite link, a "Run this check" command, the edit link pointing at the real `Test.<ID>.md`, and the metadata table folded into Details.
5. **Install command:** it follows the version picker. By default it shows `-AllowPrerelease`, so following the docs gives you the version they describe.
6. **Phone menu:** the non-docs pages now have one; they had no navigation at all on phones.
7. **Test catalog:** it opens on the most severe checks and shows 100 at a time with "Show all". On phones each check is a card. It now has styled controls, a Reset button, an empty state and a labelled "Run these checks" command.
8. **2.x archive:** it has its own sidebar and a notice that it's archived. This also fixes the stray "0" group the design review saw.
9. **Search basics:** I added `robots.txt` and a Cloudflare `_headers` file (caching, security headers, noindex for the Markdown copies and the demo). The sitemap now has dates and leaves out the blog's tag and author pages. Search skips the 2.x pages.
10. **Missing descriptions:** 81 pages were using the site-wide description and now have their own. Pages that shared a title now have distinct ones.
11. **Page structure:** the manifesto has a title, nested `<main>` elements are gone, and the 404 page is a real page.
12. **Smaller pages:** the pronunciation button no longer loads React (about 65 KB), and the video player loads only when you scroll near it.
13. **Sponsor page:** each logo was showing both its light and dark versions side by side. Google Tag Manager now loads only on maester.dev.
14. **Smaller fixes:**
    - Heading sizes and anchor offsets.
    - A focus ring in the brand colour.
    - Code blocks without the decorative three dots, and wrapping instead of clipping.
    - Command pages with sentence-case headings and a shorter "On this page" list.
    - Blog titles in the normal text colour, without emoji.
    - Three broken links fixed.

**Not done yet, roughly in order of impact:**
- Command pages still show the raw parameter metadata block, list all 23 examples, and use one flat sidebar of every command.
- The 336 Zero Trust checks aren't in the test catalog.
- Packs has no gallery landing page.
- Two test pages have a duplicate H1, and many skip from H2 to H4.
- Fonts aren't preloaded.
- Contributors pages still use emoji as icons.
- The 3.0 launch post's countdown is out of date.
- I haven't confirmed that Cloudflare accepts the `/docs/*.md` header pattern.
- The video plays live on the site but isn't rendered to MP4 for YouTube, because this machine has no FFmpeg.

# The Maester Manifesto

Maester exists to make cloud security testing open, reusable, and available to everyone.

The core idea is simple: security guidance should not only be written down. It should be executable. If a setting matters, if a risky default is buried ten pages deep in a portal, or if a standard says something should be configured a certain way, people should be able to run a test, see the result, understand the rationale, and improve.

This should not require a large budget, a specialist team, or access to expensive tooling. Individual admins, small security teams, nonprofits, schools, startups, and organizations in developing nations deserve useful security checks, too.

Security should not become another place where the gap between well-funded organizations and everyone else gets wider.

Maester exists to help close that gap.

## Open Source Core

Maester is open source and will remain open source.

The core framework will remain free. The included core tests will remain free. Running Maester locally in your own environment will remain free.

Anyone should be able to take Maester, install it, inspect it, adapt it, run it, and use it in their own workflows. That includes individual admins, internal security teams, consultants, MSPs, vendors, auditors, educators, and community contributors.

An objective of the Maester project is to minimize duplication of effort, provide a reference model across environments, and allow for that to be reused within the authority provided by the MIT license.
