content.text:
The videos now play audio, and the home video starts by itself as you scroll to it. Test list pages use the full width. The build passes, all 2,679 old URLs still resolve, and nothing is committed.

**Audio**
- **Docs videos:** "What happens in a run" and "Why a check didn't run" had no soundtrack at all. Both now have a Kokoro voice-over and the music track. After one click, the audio plays unmuted.
- **Home video:** when it scrolls into view it plays muted, with the voice-over as captions at the bottom. It pauses when you scroll away and resumes when you come back.
  - "Turn on sound" restarts it from the beginning with audio.
  - After that click, scrolling no longer stops it.
  - It never starts by itself for people who've turned on reduced motion; they get the transcript open instead.
- **Testing:** I tested the home video in headless Chromium because the browser pane was hidden and couldn't be shown in this window. While hidden, a page doesn't render, so scroll detection never fires; that's why it looked broken earlier. I also changed how the scroll detection works so it's less fragile.

**The ending:** after the automate part, the home video now ends on a Maester Cloud scene:
- Its headline reads "Or run it with Maester Cloud, in your own Azure subscription."
- Three points follow: your subscription, your data never leaves your tenant, and every run kept.
- It closes with a `maester.cloud` button and "Get started free at maester.dev".

**Test list pages:** the width fix I made earlier never took effect, because the CSS was output as literal text. It works now: `/docs/tests/asd` is 932px wide at a 1280px window (it was 736px) and 1216px at 1600px. On phones it's unchanged, with no sideways scrolling.

**Other changes**
- The home page now says **74+ contributors**, in both the stats band and the community heading. The number comes from the contributor list, so it updates itself.
- The play button now reads "Watch what happens in a run" instead of "Watch What happens…".

One thing to look at: on the closing Maester Cloud scene, the caption box covers the bottom edge of the card. That's normal for captions, but I can move the card up a little if it bothers you.

content.text:
All of it is built and running at http://localhost:4329; just reload the page. I checked everything in headless Chromium, including phone width and dark mode. Nothing is committed.

**Report demo on the home page**
- **Tabs:** they now advance on their own every 6 seconds while the demo is on screen. The highlight slides to the next tab, a red line under it fills until the switch, and the old page slides out as the new one slides in.
  - Hovering pauses it.
  - Clicking a tab or using the arrow keys takes over, and it stops switching after that.
  - It doesn't switch on its own for people who've turned on reduced motion.
  - On phones the tabs are one row that scrolls sideways and keeps the current tab in view.
- **Missing icons:** the demo was built from an older version of the report that showed letters ("Ex", "Pv", "365") for those products. The latest report build has the icons, but loads them from maester.dev, which doesn't serve them yet.
  - I copied the icons into this site under `public/report-icons/v1` and made the demo load them from there.
  - I rebuilt the demo from the latest report and re-captured all 12 screenshots. Exchange, Purview and Microsoft 365 now show their icons.

**Hero row**
- The command box and both buttons are now the same 48px height. I removed the note under the command; the banner at the top already says it's the 3.0 preview.
- The line underneath now reads "Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux · Nothing leaves your tenant".

**Test catalog** ([localhost:4329/docs/tests](http://localhost:4329/docs/tests))
- **Suites and severities** are now on/off chips with icons, and you can pick several at once.
  - Severity icons are signal bars in the severity's colour.
  - Suites about one product show that product's icon, CIS, CISA and ASD get line icons, and Maester shows its flame.
- **Product and feature** is a searchable menu with a tree. Expand a product to tick its features; ticking a product ticks all of them, and a partly ticked product shows a dash. Searching "conditional" opens Entra ID straight to Conditional Access.
- **Area** is a searchable menu too. "New in 3.0" is a chip.
- **The command** builds from every filter, for example `Invoke-Maester -Product entra -Feature conditional-access -Area authentication -Severity High`. `-Feature` only matches by name, and 11 feature names exist under more than one product, so the command always adds the product.
- **Links:** the filters go into the page URL, so a filtered view can be shared. Old links like `?product=entra&suite=CIS` still work.
- **Product column:** it stays on one line now, with the product's icon.
- **Native dropdowns:** none are left anywhere on the site. Test builder already used rich dropdowns.

**Test builder**
- It's now a tab in the top nav (Guides · Test catalog · Test builder · Commands…).
- It opens in the docs layout, with the left nav showing Test builder and the writing-your-own-tests guides, and uses the full width.
- It keeps its `/test-builder` URL.

**ReUI:** I used ReUI's filter and searchable-dropdown designs as the model rather than installing them. They're React components that need Tailwind and shadcn, which would clash with the docs theme, so the catalog builds them itself with the site's own styles.

**Before merging:** the report redesign branch puts these icons in `website/static/report-icons/`, the old Docusaurus folder. This site serves them from `website/public/report-icons/`, so that branch should use the new folder.

Maester 3.0 merges into main on Thursday, 8 October 2026 at 10:00 UTC (8 pm AEST). From that moment the preview build of Maester on the PowerShell Gallery is Maester 3.0, and 3.0 has breaking changes.

If you run Maester in automation with the preview build, switch to the release build now

Your next scheduled run after the merge will pick up 3.0. The biggest change is that Maester 3.0 needs PowerShell 7.4 or later. Windows PowerShell 5.1 is no longer supported. We’ve worked hard to keep your custom tests (including Pester tests) working, but a rewrite this size will have rough edges.

You’re on the preview build if your pipeline does any of these:

  • Install-Module Maester -AllowPrerelease or Update-Module Maester -AllowPrerelease
  • maester_version: preview in the Maester GitHub Action

To stay on 2.x, install the release build instead: drop -AllowPrerelease, or pin the version with Install-Module Maester -RequiredVersion 2.3.0. In the GitHub Action, use maester_version: latest.

NowMove automation off the preview build
8 Oct, 10:00 UTC3.0 merges into main and becomes the preview build
After thatWe fix what the preview finds, then ship 3.0 as the release build

If you’re using Maester interactively and want to see what’s coming, the preview is exactly where we want you. Try it, and tell us what breaks.

Maester 3.0
Its own test engine. Pester optional.

Every built-in security check is now a plain PowerShell function with its metadata attached. Maester reads that metadata to decide what runs, a small engine runs it, and the results keep the 2.x shape.

747native tests
0built-in Pester files
64exported commands (2.x: ~730)
7.4+PowerShell

This post has two halves. The first half covers what most of you will notice: you no longer install a tests folder, and the way a test is written has changed. The second half is the technical detail for people who build pipelines on Maester, write a lot of custom tests, or just want to know how it works.

All of this is live at http://localhost:4329 and not committed. I couldn't listen to the audio or see the blur from here (headless screenshots don't draw it), so please check both in your browser.

**Home video**
- **No autoplay:** it now waits behind the big red play button. Clicking starts it with sound from the beginning.
- **Behind the button:** a blurred copy of the title card shows, instead of an empty black frame.
- **Start delay:** the voice now begins 0.3 seconds in (it was 1.2 seconds), the music fades in within half a second, and the title appears straight away. In a test, playback was running within 1.5 seconds of the click.
- **Crackling:** the audio didn't clip, so I fixed the likely causes in the scripts that make it, then regenerated all three explainers:
  - The background chords switched abruptly at every bar line, which clicked about every 2.7 seconds. They now crossfade.
  - Bass and arpeggio notes were cut off mid-wave, which clicked. They now fade out.
  - The voice was converted to a higher sample rate in a crude way that adds a fizz on "s" and "t" sounds. It now uses a cleaner conversion.
  - Each voice line now fades in and out over a few milliseconds, and the MP3s are encoded at 192 kbps instead of 128.

**Blog**
- **Same header as Contributors**, no left nav. The docs header still has a Blog tab that links to it.
- **Index:** the newest post is a large featured card, and every other post is a big clickable card with its picture, type, date, summary, authors and reading time. A row of topics (Release, Azure DevOps, Microsoft 365…) and an RSS link sit at the top; on phones the topics scroll sideways in one row.
- **Posts:** one centred column about 70 characters wide in larger text. Posts with three or more sections get a sticky "On this page" list on wide screens. The end of each post has the topics, Discord and "Write for the blog" links, and "Keep reading" cards for the posts either side.
- **Same URLs:** topic, author and RSS pages keep their old addresses, and old `/blog/page/2` links now go to `/blog`.
- **One change you'll see:** all 25 posts are on one page now; there's no second page.

**Bug fixed along the way:** the `:::note` and `:::caution` boxes weren't working anywhere, docs included. They came out as plain text, because the content lives outside the folder Starlight processes by default. I listed the content folders in the Starlight config, and they now render as proper callouts on both the docs and the blog.

The main new files are [src/pages/blog/](.claude/worktrees/website-astro/website/src/pages/blog), [src/components/blog/PostCard.astro](.claude/worktrees/website-astro/website/src/components/blog/PostCard.astro), [src/lib/blog.ts](.claude/worktrees/website-astro/website/src/lib/blog.ts) and [src/styles/blog-prose.css](.claude/worktrees/website-astro/website/src/styles/blog-prose.css). ---
description: "This is the main Maester command that runs the tests and generates a report of the results."
title: Invoke-Maester
editUrl: https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/public/run/Invoke-Maester.ps1
---

## SYNOPSIS

This is the main Maester command that runs the tests and generates a report of the results.

## SYNTAX

```powershell
Invoke-Maester [[-Path] <String>] [-Tag <String[]>] [-ExcludeTag <String[]>] [-Product <String[]>]
 [-ExcludeProduct <String[]>] [-Feature <String[]>] [-Area <String[]>] [-Severity <String[]>]
 [-Suite <String[]>] [-Pack <String[]>] [-AllPacks] [-IncludeLongRunning] [-IncludePreview]
 [-OutputHtmlFile <String>] [-IncludeAffectedObjects] [-RedactUserIdentity <String>]
 [-OutputMarkdownFile <String>] [-OutputMarkdownSummaryFile <String>] [-OutputJsonFile <String>]
 [-OutputFolder <String>] [-OutputFolderFileName <String>] [-PesterConfiguration <Object>]
 [-Verbosity <String>] [-NonInteractive] [-PassThru] [-MailRecipient <String[]>] [-MailTestResultsUri <String>]
 [-MailUserId <String>] [-TeamId <String>] [-TeamChannelId <String>] [-TeamChannelWebhookUri <String>]
 [-SkipGraphConnect] [-DisableTelemetry] [-SkipVersionCheck] [-ExportCsv] [-ExportExcel] [-NoLogo]
 [-OutputMode <String>] [-DriftRoot <String>] [-TestId <String[]>] [-ExcludeTestId <String[]>]
 [-Config <Object>] [-DryRun] [-SkipBuiltIn] [-PackLock <String>] [-SkipPack]
 [-ProgressAction <ActionPreference>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

Using Invoke-Maester is the easiest way to run the Pester tests and generate a report of the results.

For more advanced configuration, you can directly use the Pester module and the Get-MtHtmlReport function.

By default, Invoke-Maester runs the tests that ship with Maester and the custom tests in the Custom folder of the current directory, except Active Directory tests, preview tests and long-running tests.
With -Path, native custom tests (Test.*.ps1) are found anywhere under the path and Pester-format custom tests (*.Tests.ps1) only in a Custom folder.
Folders are searched up to three levels deep.
Active Directory tests run only after an explicit Connect-Maester -Service ActiveDirectory call succeeds.

-Product, -Feature, -Area, -Severity and -Suite select tests by their typed attributes.
Each takes a list: the values of one selector are alternatives, and different selectors must all match.
They combine the same way with -Tag and -TestId.
-ExcludeProduct leaves out the tests of a product and wins over every selector.
The tags of Maester 2.x, such as CA or CIS, still select the same built-in tests.

## EXAMPLES

### EXAMPLE 1

```powershell
Invoke-Maester
```

Runs the built-in tests and the custom tests in the ./Custom folder (except for Active Directory tests, preview tests and long-running tests) and generates a report of the results in the ./test-results folder.

### EXAMPLE 2

```powershell
Invoke-Maester ./maester
```

content.text:
I've made all of your command-page changes. They're live at http://localhost:4329/docs/commands and not committed.

**Command pages**
- **More room:** the content column is now wider, and the right pane is narrower and further right, since its list is short. At a 1440px window the syntax lines now almost fit without scrolling.
- **Syntax block:** it keeps the line breaks the help file has, one group of parameters per line, instead of breaking inside a parameter like `[-` / `Product`. If it runs past 5 lines it shows the first 5 with a fade and a **Show full syntax** button, so the description below is in view.
- **Long names:** titles use a smaller font. Names over 26 characters get smaller still, so `Get-MtUserAuthenticationMethodInfoByType` fits on one line and no longer runs under the Copy page button.

**Left nav**
- **By job (the default):** it starts with **Start here**, showing **Connect-Maester** and **Invoke-Maester** in bold with a red dot. Then come the groups, taken from the module's own folders:
  - Connect
  - Run and write tests
  - Reports and alerts
  - Maester Packs
  - Automation setup
  - Entra and Microsoft Graph
  - Exchange and email
  - Azure and SharePoint
  - Active Directory

  The four service groups start collapsed and open when you're on one of their pages.
- **A to Z:** a switch at the top lists every command alphabetically. Your choice is remembered.
- **One line per name:** long names end in an ellipsis, and the full name shows on hover.

**Commands overview**
- **Two key commands up top:** large cards, "Step 1 · Sign in" for Connect-Maester and "Step 2 · Run the checks" for Invoke-Maester.
- **Groups:** a row of group chips with counts, then each group with a line on what it's for and a card per command. "On this page" now lists the groups.
- **Keeping it in sync:** the groups come from the folder each command lives in. A new command lands in the right group by itself, and one in a new folder shows under "Other" until it's added to [command-groups.mjs](.claude/worktrees/website-astro/website/src/lib/command-groups.mjs).

One thing I noticed: in Invoke-Maester's description, `Test.*.ps1` and `*.Tests.ps1` turn part of a sentence into italics. The `*` characters come from the comment-based help in the module source. That page is generated, so the fix belongs in the source and not in the website files.
Yes, fix the help

input.content:
## 📑 Description

Rebuilds maester.dev on **Astro 7 + Starlight**, replacing Docusaurus. Every URL the old site had still resolves: `src/data/url-contract.txt` (2,679 URLs) is checked on every build, and `dist/_redirects` is generated for Cloudflare Pages.

**Docs**
- Docs default to the 3.0 preview. Pages mark what differs from the stable release, and the 2.x guides are kept as an archive at `/docs/2.x`. The 2.x command and test pages are dropped; their URLs redirect to the current pages.
- `:::note` / `:::caution` callouts now render. The content lives outside `src/content/docs`, so Starlight needs the folders named in `markdown.processedDirs`.

**Test catalog** (`/docs/tests`)
- Generated from `src/data/test-catalog.json`.
- Filters: a searchable product → feature tree, area, suite and severity toggles. A copyable `Invoke-Maester` command matches the filters.

**Commands** (`/docs/commands`)
- Grouped by job, from the module's folders (connect, run, report, packs, app, services/*), with an A to Z switch in the sidebar.
- Connect-Maester and Invoke-Maester come first. Long syntax blocks collapse behind "Show full syntax", and pages are wider.

**Blog**
- Its own content collection on the site layout, with no docs sidebar.
- Card index, reading-width posts, topic and author pages, and RSS at `/blog/rss.xml`. `starlight-blog` is removed.

**Home page**
- The real 3.0 HTML report as a live demo, with auto-rotating views.
- A click-to-play HyperFrames explainer with a Kokoro voice-over and synthesised music. The audio tools in `website/scripts/narration` are not part of the build.

**Test builder** has its own header tab, inside the docs layout.

**Module help**
- `Invoke-Maester`: backticks around `Test.*.ps1` / `*.Tests.ps1`, which rendered as italics.
- `Invoke-MtGraphRequest`: `:::note` instead of the unsupported `:::info`.
- Command pages regenerated with `./build/Update-CommandReference.ps1`.

## ✅ Checks

- [x] My pull request adheres to the code style of this project.
- [x] My code requires changes to the documentation.
- [x] I have updated the documentation as required.
- [ ] The build and unit tests pass after running `/powershell/tests/pester.ps1` locally. 6,566 of 6,567 pass. The one failure is local: `ZeroTrustAssessmentPack.Tests.ps1` expects the ZeroTrustAssessment module not to be installed, and it is on the machine that ran them. This PR changes only two lines of help text in the module.

## ℹ️ Additional Information

Before merging:
- **Cloudflare Pages settings must change:** build output `website/dist`, Node 24. The `build-docs.yaml` and `publish-versioned-docs.yml` workflows are removed; `build-website.yaml` builds the new site.
- **Customer story:** the Xbox story stays hidden until `src/data/media.json` has an approved date. The quotes need sign-off from Audrey Long and Microsoft.
- **Report icons:** `website/public/report-icons/v1` is copied from the report redesign work, which keeps them in `website/static/report-icons/`. Reconcile the two locations when that work lands.

content.text:
I fixed the CodeQL alert on PR #2647, pushed the fix as `8247f17b7`, and replied in the review thread and resolved it. CI still has to run on the new commit.

- **The problem:** `website/src/lib/summary.mjs` turns Markdown into the plain text used for page descriptions, and it removed HTML comments in a single pass. A crafted string like `<!<!---->--` would come out as a new `<!--`, which is what CodeQL flagged.
- **The fix:** it now removes comments over and over until nothing changes. Then it drops any `<!--`, `-->`, `{/*` or `*/}` left without its partner.
- **Checked:** the crafted string now comes out clean, normal summaries are unchanged, the site builds, and all old URLs still resolve.

content.text:
I fixed both failing checks on PR #2647 and pushed them as `06370359d`. CI hasn't rerun on the new commit yet.

- **Website build:** CI's clean install (`npm ci`) didn't include `@astrojs/markdown-remark`, which the site's Markdown plugins need. Astro, Starlight and MDX only list it as an optional peer, so it was only present locally because of an earlier install. It's now a pinned direct dependency (7.3.5). After deleting `node_modules` and running `npm ci`, the site builds and all old URLs still resolve.
- **CodeQL (two new alerts on the same line):** my earlier fix still used a regular expression, and it missed comments that end with `--!>`. Comment removal in `summary.mjs` now scans the text without a regex:
  - each `<!--` ends at the first `-->` or `--!>`;
  - a comment with no end runs to the end of the text, as it does in HTML;
  - the scan repeats until no opener is left.

  The tricky inputs all come out clean, and normal summaries are unchanged. I replied in both review threads and resolved them.

The build also prints a deprecation warning: Astro now wants the remark and rehype plugins passed a different way. It doesn't fail the build, so I've left the config as it is.

         const { open, close, at } = found.reduce((a, b) => (b.at < a.at ? b : a));

# Refreshes the people on maester.dev/sponsor (the contributors who have a GitHub Sponsors listing) and the sponsors

name: Update sponsor page

on:

jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # The maester-bot app, not GITHUB_TOKEN: it looks up the Sponsors listing of each contributor over

      - name: Generate maester-bot app token

---
# Validates that the website (Astro + Starlight) builds, and that every URL of the old site still resolves.
# Runs on PRs that modify website files or docs source files, and can also be
# called from other workflows or triggered manually.
name: "\U0001F3D7️ Build Website"

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      node_version:
        description: "Node.js version to use."
        required: false
        default: "24.x"
        type: string
      working_directory:
        description: "Path to the directory containing package.json (relative to the repository root)."
        required: false
        default: "website"
        type: string
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
    branches: ["main"]
    paths:
      - "build/Update-CommandReference.ps1"
      - "build/eidsca/*.json"
      - "powershell/**"
      - "tests/**"
      - "website/**"
      - ".github/workflows/build-website.yaml"

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  detect-command-reference-changes:
    name: "Detect command reference changes"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      generate: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || steps.filter.outputs.command_reference == 'true' }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Check command reference inputs
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        id: filter
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@ceb8a2b8f2d89434be7ff52d3de7ec3738c5cc9d # v4.0.3
        with:
          filters: |
            command_reference:
              - "build/Update-CommandReference.ps1"
              - "powershell/**"
              - "tests/**"
              - ".github/workflows/build-website.yaml"

  generate-command-reference:
    name: "Generate command reference"
    needs: detect-command-reference-changes
    if: needs.detect-command-reference-changes.outputs.generate == 'true'
    runs-on: windows-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Generate command reference
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./build/Update-CommandReference.ps1

      - name: Package generated command reference
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ProgressPreference = "SilentlyContinue"
          $artifactRoot = Join-Path $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE "generated-command-reference"
          $docsRoot = Join-Path $artifactRoot "docs"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $docsRoot -Force | Out-Null

          $sourceCommands = Join-Path $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE "website/docs/commands"
          if (-not (Test-Path $sourceCommands)) {
            throw "Command reference docs were not generated at $sourceCommands."
          }

          Copy-Item -Path $sourceCommands -Destination $docsRoot -Recurse -Force

          Compress-Archive -Path (Join-Path $artifactRoot "*") -DestinationPath command-reference-docs.zip -Force

      - name: Upload generated command reference
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: generated-command-reference
          path: command-reference-docs.zip
          if-no-files-found: error

  build:
    name: "Build website \U0001F3D7️"
    needs: [detect-command-reference-changes, generate-command-reference]
    if: always() && needs.detect-command-reference-changes.result == 'success' && (needs.generate-command-reference.result == 'success' || needs.generate-command-reference.result == 'skipped')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: ⬇️ Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Full history so contributor profiles get display names and first-contribution dates from git.
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Download generated command reference
        if: needs.detect-command-reference-changes.outputs.generate == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: generated-command-reference
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/command-reference

      - name: Apply generated command reference
        if: needs.detect-command-reference-changes.outputs.generate == 'true'
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          WEBSITE_WORKING_DIRECTORY: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}
        run: |
          $ProgressPreference = "SilentlyContinue"
          Remove-Item -Path (Join-Path $env:WEBSITE_WORKING_DIRECTORY "docs/commands") -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

          Expand-Archive -Path "${{ runner.temp }}/command-reference/command-reference-docs.zip" -DestinationPath $env:WEBSITE_WORKING_DIRECTORY -Force

      - name: ⚙️ Set up Node.js ${{ inputs.node_version || '24.x' }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node_version || '24.x' }}
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}/package-lock.json

      - name: "\U0001F4E6 Install dependencies"
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}
        run: npm ci

      # The test pages are built from the test catalog, exported from the source module (Get-MtTest), which needs
      # this module to import. Exporting it here means a PR's new or changed tests render in this build.
      - name: Install Microsoft.Graph.Authentication for the test catalog export
        shell: pwsh
        run: Install-Module Microsoft.Graph.Authentication -MinimumVersion 2.27.0 -Scope CurrentUser -Repository PSGallery -Force

      - name: Export the test catalog
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}
        run: npm run export-catalog

      # npm run build also checks every URL in website/src/data/url-contract.txt against the output.
      - name: "\U0001F3D7️ Build website"
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

input.recap: All three workflows are still needed on the new site, because Cloudflare builds only from files committed to the repo. They need you to merge by hand because the main ruleset requires a human approval. Building and deploying the site from GitHub Actions would remove all three PRs. Nothing has been changed yet.
input.ask: Should I switch the site to deploy from GitHub Actions so these PRs go away?

content.text:
**Short answer:** yes, all three are still needed as things stand. Each one exists only because Cloudflare Pages builds from what's committed to the repo, and it can't run PowerShell or use the bot's token to call GitHub. If the site is built and deployed from GitHub Actions instead, none of the three has to open a PR.

**Why they're still needed today**

| Workflow | What it commits | Why it's still needed |
|---|---|---|
| `update-sponsors` (daily) | `src/data/sponsors.json` and the Sponsors section of `README.md` | The sponsor page reads that JSON. Finding out which people have a Sponsors listing needs GitHub's API with the bot's token. |
| `update-module-docs` | `website/docs/commands/*.mdx` | The command pages are built from those files. Generating them needs PowerShell and PlatyPS, and the job runs on a Windows runner. |
| `update-test-docs` | `src/data/test-catalog.json`, `contributors.json`, `email-aliases.json` | The test pages and contributor credits are built from those files. The export needs PowerShell, and the credits need the full git history. |

One thing has already changed with the new site: there are no generated test pages in git any more (`website/docs/tests` is gone). Only the JSON catalog is committed.

**Why you have to merge them by hand:** the `main` ruleset requires one approving review and approval of the last push. A bot PR can never meet that on its own. Turning on auto-merge wouldn't fix it, and auto-merge is also switched off on the repo.

**Options**

1. **Deploy from GitHub Actions (recommended).** On every push to `main`, plus once a day for sponsors, a workflow would:
   - export the catalog;
   - generate the command pages;
   - work out contributors and sponsors with the bot's token;
   - build the site;
   - upload it to Cloudflare with `wrangler pages deploy`.

   The generated files stop being committed and get ignored by git. This removes all three PRs and the noise they add to the diffs. Most of these steps are already in `build-website.yaml`, which runs them on every PR to check the build.

   The README sponsor section is the one piece that still writes to git. It could show an image the site generates (`https://maester.dev/sponsors.svg`, or similar), so the README itself never has to change.

   **What you'd need to do:** add a Cloudflare API token as a repo secret and turn off Cloudflare's own builds from git. This also replaces the change to the Cloudflare Pages build settings that's already pending for this PR.
2. **Keep the PRs but let them merge themselves.** Add the maester-bot app as a bypass actor on the ruleset, limited to these generated paths if possible, and turn on auto-merge. This is less work, but generated files keep landing in `main`, and the bypass is a security setting only you can change.

If you choose option 1, the change could go into PR #2647 or a follow-up PR. I'd also update the "Generated content" rule in AGENTS.md to match.
Yes, do it here

input.content:
# Builds maester.dev (Astro + Starlight) and checks that every URL of the old site still resolves. On a pull
# request it only builds; on main, daily and on request it also deploys the build to Cloudflare Pages.
#
# The site's generated data is not kept in git: the build exports the test catalog and the command reference from
# the module source, credits contributors from the git history and looks up sponsors on GitHub
# (website/scripts/prepare-data.mjs). So a merge needs no follow-up pull request, and the daily run picks up new
# sponsors.
#
# Deploying needs the CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN secret (a token with Cloudflare Pages: Edit) and the
# CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID secret in the maester.dev environment. The Cloudflare Pages project, which the
# CLOUDFLARE_PAGES_PROJECT variable can name (default: maester), must not also build from git.
name: "\U0001F3D7️ Build Website"

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      node_version:
        description: "Node.js version to use."
        required: false
        default: "24.x"
        type: string
      working_directory:
        description: "Path to the directory containing package.json (relative to the repository root)."
        required: false
        default: "website"
        type: string
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 3 * * *" # Daily, 03:17 UTC: new sponsors
  push:
    branches: ["main"]
  pull_request:
    branches: ["main"]
    paths:
      - "README.md"
      - "build/Update-CommandReference.ps1"
      - "build/docs/**"
      - "build/eidsca/*.json"
      - "powershell/**"
      - "tests/**"
      - "website/**"
      - ".github/workflows/build-website.yaml"

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions: {}

jobs:
  build:
    name: "Build website \U0001F3D7️"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}

    steps:
      # On main, the maester-bot app's token: it may read whether each contributor has a GitHub Sponsors listing
      # and who sponsors the maintainers. A pull request build uses the repository's token, which may not, and
      # shows the sponsors of the last deploy.
      - name: Generate maester-bot app token
        id: app-token
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.MAESTER_BOT_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.MAESTER_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: ⬇️ Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Full history so contributor profiles get display names and first-contribution dates from git.
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: ⚙️ Set up Node.js ${{ inputs.node_version || '24.x' }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node_version || '24.x' }}
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}/package-lock.json

      - name: "\U0001F4E6 Install dependencies"
        run: npm ci

      # The test catalog export imports the source module, which needs this module.
      - name: Install Microsoft.Graph.Authentication
        shell: pwsh
        run: Install-Module Microsoft.Graph.Authentication -MinimumVersion 2.27.0 -Scope CurrentUser -Repository PSGallery -Force

      # npm run build first generates the site's data (scripts/prepare-data.mjs), then checks every URL in
      # website/src/data/url-contract.txt against the output.
      - name: "\U0001F3D7️ Build website"
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
        run: npm run build

      # The README's Sponsors section is written from website/sponsors/featured.yml.
      - name: Check the README's Sponsors section
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: |
          node scripts/sponsors.mjs --readme
          git diff --exit-code -- ../README.md || { echo "::error file=README.md::The Sponsors section is out of date. Run: cd website && node scripts/sponsors.mjs --readme"; exit 1; }

      - name: Upload the site
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: website
          path: ${{ inputs.working_directory || 'website' }}/dist
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to maester.dev
    needs: build
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.repository == 'maester365/maester'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    environment:
      name: maester.dev
      url: https://maester.dev

    steps:
      - name: Download the site
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: website
          path: dist

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24.x

      - name: Deploy to Cloudflare Pages
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          PROJECT: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_PAGES_PROJECT || 'maester' }}
          COMMIT: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: npx --yes wrangler@4.151.2 pages deploy dist --project-name "$PROJECT" --branch main --commit-hash "$COMMIT" --commit-dirty=true

## Hard rules

- Generated content — regenerate, never hand-edit: `website/docs/commands/`,
  `website/src/data/test-catalog.json` (the test pages are built from it),
  `website/src/data/versions.json`, `website/versioned_docs/` (the frozen 2.x docs), everything under
  `powershell/internal/generated/`, and the native `tests/eidsca/Test.EIDSCA.*` and
  `tests/orca/Test.ORCA.*` files the generators in `build/eidsca/` and `build/orca/`
  write. Edit the PowerShell source, comment-based help or generator templates and let
  automation regenerate. `powershell/assets/ConsoleContributors.json` (the dashboard's
  Featured contributor list) is written by `./build/Update-ConsoleContributors.ps1` from
  the website's contributor data.
- A test is mapped to a framework in one place: the `Control` attribute, `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>`. A
  CIS test carries `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'`, a CISA test `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'`, and any other
----

## Where things are

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/` | The guides and the command reference (`docs/commands`, generated by `build/Update-CommandReference.ps1`). A file's path is its URL. |
| `blog/` | Blog posts, one folder each. |
| `versioned_docs/version-2.3.0/` | The Maester 2.x docs, frozen, served at `/docs/2.x` with `noindex`. |
| `src/data/test-catalog.json` | Every built-in test, exported by `npm run export-catalog`. The test pages and the catalog are built from it at build time by `scripts/generate-test-docs.mjs` (into the ignored `.generated/`). |
| `src/data/versions.json` | The release each test, command and parameter first shipped in. With `version-config.js` it decides what is marked **Preview**. |
| `src/data/url-contract.txt` | Every URL the site had before the move to Astro. The build fails if one stops resolving. |
| `src/lib/redirects.mjs` | Writes `dist/_redirects` (Cloudflare Pages) for the URLs that moved. |
| `src/lib/content-loader.ts` | Loads the guides, tests, 2.x archive and blog into Starlight with the URLs they had on Docusaurus. |
| `src/components/` | Starlight overrides (`overrides/`), the version picker, the test catalog, the explainer player and the other components. |
| `src/pages/` | The pages outside the docs: home, sponsor, contributors, manifesto, test builder, EIDSCA sync. |
| `public/explainers/` | The HyperFrames explainers: HTML and GSAP, played live by `<Explainer>`. |

----
## Contributing to Maester docs and blog posts

Simple edits can be made in the GitHub UI by selecting the `Edit this page` link at the bottom of each page or you can browse to the [docs](https://github.com/maester365/maester/tree/main/website/docs) folder on GitHub.

For more complex changes, you can fork the repository and submit a pull request.

The docs/commands folder is auto-generated based on the comments in the PowerShell cmdlets. If you want to update the documentation for a command, you will need to update the comment-based help in the .ps1 file for the command.

### Running documentation locally

The [Maester.dev](https://maester.dev) website is built with [Astro](https://astro.build) and [Starlight](https://starlight.astro.build).
- A page that uses components (tabs, icons, explainers) is an `.mdx` file and imports them, for example
  `import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';` or
  `import IIcon from '@components/IIcon.astro';` for an [Iconify](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/) icon. See
  [Starlight's components](https://starlight.astro.build/components/using-components/).
- The pages under `Commands` are generated from each command's comment-based help: edit the `.ps1` file, not the page.
- The test pages are built from each test's `[MaesterTest]` attribute and `Test.<ID>.md`: edit those, not the
  website. `npm run export-catalog` refreshes `website/src/data/test-catalog.json` from your local tests (it needs
  PowerShell 7 and the `Microsoft.Graph.Authentication` module).

#### Stable and preview

The docs describe the preview, which is published to the PowerShell Gallery each time a change is merged. Checks,
commands and parameters that the stable release doesn't have are marked **Preview** automatically, from the test

3. Identities are matched to GitHub accounts automatically: GitHub noreply

Attribution works with zero setup, but you can enrich your profile card:

| `needs rebase` | `mergeable` is `CONFLICTING`. Remove it when the conflict is gone. | Triage |
| `generated` | Every changed file is generated, as in the bot PRs that refresh the test catalog. Generated files are `website/src/data/test-catalog.json`, `website/src/data/contributors.json`, `website/src/data/versions.json`, `website/docs/commands/**`, `website/versioned_docs/**`, `**/fixtures/golden/**`, `website/src/data/test-builder.json`, `packs/*/catalog.json`, the upstream-generated suites `tests/eidsca/**`, `tests/orca/**` and `powershell/internal/generated/**`, the agent and skill copies `.claude/agents/**`, `.claude/skills/**` and `website/docs/agents-and-skills.md` that `build/github/Update-AgentFiles.ps1` writes, `*.dll`, lock files, and any other file whose first lines contain both "Generated by" and "Do not edit". | Triage |
| `breaking change` | It removes or renames a public cmdlet, parameter, output field or test ID, changes a default, removes a check from the default run, or changes what a check considers correct. Fixing a check so that it matches its documented behaviour is a `bug`, not a breaking change. On an issue: the request or the reported fix would need such a change. | Triage adds; only a maintainer removes |
